Assume Countable Choice. Let two balanced multipointed Heegaard diagrams be compatible with the same oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Each has its actual embedded splitting, simultaneous trivial-arc systems and compression data, a genus-$h$ surface, $k\ge1$ ordered pairs $w_i,z_i$, and $m=h+k-1$ curves in each attaching system. The lower arcs run from $w_i$ to $z_i$ and the upper arcs from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with cyclic indices. The two diagrams may have different genera and different numbers of pairs. Include the full smooth input convention allowing tangential marked knot crossings and auxiliary proper compression-disk witnesses; no additional neatness hypothesis is imposed.

There is a finite comparison between them using curve isotopies and same-system handleslides avoiding all marks, genus-one stabilizations or destabilizations in knot-disjoint disks, and actual basepoint-pair stabilizations or destabilizations along the represented knot. The latter keep the genus fixed and change $k$ by one; their inverse configuration consists of surface disks bounded by $\alpha_0,\beta_0$ meeting twice and no other opposite-system curve, with their common bigon containing just the new $w_0$, the first disk outside the second containing just the new $z_0$, and the second outside the first containing the next old $z$-point in the cyclic pairing. Removing that configuration concatenates the adjacent actual trivial arcs. Thus no isolated marked knot component is added in an empty disk.

The comparison permits the explicit orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms carrying the ordered marks, attaching systems and actual arc systems, and the fixed-splitting arc normalizations of the pointed-data definition, before or after its geometric moves. Every intermediate geometric diagram remains balanced with $m=h+k-1$, the same oriented knot, and the stated simultaneous bridge data. It is admissible in that definition's integral periodic-domain sense. The case $k=1$, including $h=0,m=0$, is included. This theorem establishes geometric move generation; it makes no assertion about analytic continuation maps or disk counts.

Assume countable choice. Take a balanced multipointed diagram for one oriented knot in $S^3$ with the splitting, compression disks and cyclic marking convention of the balanced pointed-data definition, without assuming its admissibility. Write $A_i$ and $B_i$ for the components of the complements of the two attaching systems, numbered so that $w_i,z_i\in A_i$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}\in B_i$, with cyclic indices, $1\le i\le k$.

Every integral domain $P$ whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching curves has an integral representation
$$P=\sum_{i=1}^k a_iA_i+\sum_{i=1}^k b_iB_i.$$
If $n_{w_i}(P)=0$ for every $i$, then $b_i=-a_i$ and
$$n_{z_i}(P)=a_i-a_{i-1},\qquad \sum_i n_{z_i}(P)=0.$$
Such a domain is zero if all its $z$ multiplicities vanish. Consequently every nonzero such domain has both a positive and a negative region coefficient: the diagram is admissible in the precise periodic-domain sense of that Definition. In particular every balanced knot diagram appearing in a valid knot-preserving multipointed move sequence in $S^3$ is admissible, without a further winding modification. This assertion does not construct the move sequence or analytic moduli spaces.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $k\ge1$ cyclically ordered mark pairs, $m=h+k-1$, transverse attaching systems and complete compression disks cutting the two handlebodies into $k$ balls. Broad auxiliary proper disk witnesses are permitted. Label the cut components by $A_i$ containing $w_i,z_i$ and $B_i$ containing $w_i,z_{i+1}$, cyclically.

There is a choice of integrable surface background, protected nearly symmetric geometry, common exact generator charts and ONE smooth tame path constant on genuine positive time collars, with no nonconstant strip of index at most zero, for which every actual nonconstant strip of index one or two is regular and there are finitely many index-one translation orbits across ALL generators, realized classes and nonnegative $w,z$ vectors. No $n_z=0$ restriction is imposed. Its endpoint unit boundary disks are regular and finite at every generator. Their mod-two counts are one for each $A_i,B_i$ when $k\ge2$, and zero for the single alpha and beta components when $k=1$; in the latter case unit spheres through the generators are excluded as in the singly pointed construction.

Let $C$ be the free module on the finite generator set over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$. The ACTUAL differential
$$d x=\sum_{y,\,[u]\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_1(x,y)}U_1^{n_{w_1}(u)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(u)}\,y$$
counts all the above index-one orbits, including every positive $z$ multiplicity. It is a finite polynomial matrix, $d^2=0$, and it preserves the relative Alexander filtration with each $U_i$ lowering filtration by one. Identifying or localizing variables by any ring homomorphism preserves this identity.

For $k\ge2$, retaining separate $V_i$ weights for $z_i$ gives the actual full-marked curvature identity
$$D^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^kU_i(V_i+V_{i+1})\right)I.$$
For $k=1$ the corresponding full-marked $D$ has $D^2=0$ by the zero unit counts. These are chosen-data analytic count identities. Comparison to other paths or diagrams, absolute gradings, analytic/combinatorial identification and Floer invariance are not input or conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed diagram of an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $m=h+k-1$, its surface complex structure and common product-integrable generator charts. Every two actual generators $x,y$ are joined by an actual continuous Whitney class. For $m>0$, the actual index and marked degrees define consistent relative integer gradings: if the generator set is nonempty, there are functions $M,A$ on it satisfying, for EVERY realized class $u:x\to y$,
$$M(x)-M(y)=\mu(u)-2\sum_i n_{w_i}(u),\qquad A(x)-A(y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(u)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(u).$$
Each function is unique up to one common additive constant. In particular every actual index-one term weighted by $U_1^{a_1}\cdots U_k^{a_k}$, where $a_i=n_{w_i}(u)$, lowers $M$ by one and lowers $A$ by exactly $\sum_i n_{z_i}(u)$ when each $U_i$ has degrees $(-2,-1)$. Positive $z$ degrees are included.

No holomorphic representative is required for Whitney connectivity. No absolute normalization, nonemptiness of the generator set, existence of regular counts, square-zero or invariant comparison is asserted. For $m=0$ the point target has its sole generator and constant class, with arbitrary constant gradings.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix one actual balanced multipointed diagram of an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $k\ge1$, $m=h+k-1$ and its ordered marks. Take two actual finite square-zero full minus count complexes over $R=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$, with all positive z degrees retained. Suppose their chosen end paths have no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and every index-one strip is regular, as in the full-marked chosen-count construction. Background surface complex structures, positive area forms, full torus tensors and optional generator charts may have been chosen independently.

There are finite actual anchored continuation matrices over R and inverse chain homotopies. They are filtered for the relative Alexander filtration and homogeneous for the relative Maslov degree, after identifying the origins on the SAME geometric generator set. Every $U_i$ has degrees $(-2,-1)$. Positive z terms are included and lower filtration by their total z degree; no associated-graded substitution is made. Scalar restriction to any chosen variable, or identification or localization of variables, preserves these actual finite identities.

The proof supplies compact low-dimensional continuation spaces and their exhaustive collars by an actual full-marked index budget. No zero-basepoint bubble exclusion is substituted for that budget. No comparison of different attaching systems, genus changes, basepoint-pair cones or absolute normalization is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed knot diagram in $S^3$ with $m=h+k-1$, its ordered marks and actual good square-zero full minus count data. For an attaching-circle handleslide or isotopy avoiding the other circles of its family and all marks, preserving the balanced knot data, the two full filtered minus complexes have finite actual chain maps and inverse chain homotopies over $R=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$. Counts include ALL positive z degrees; the variables and their marked-point actions are retained individually. A supplied finite word of such moves and pointed diagram isomorphisms gives the corresponding finite equivalence. The maps specialize or restrict to any chosen-variable module by the actual ring operation.

Maslov homogeneity and the Alexander filtration are relative: choose the origins by the actual small comparison triangles and continuous class transports in the proof. Maps have degree zero, homotopies degree plus one, and every $U_i$ has degrees $(-2,-1)$. This supplies a relative filtered comparison, not its Seifert-surface centering or absolute Maslov normalization. It proves neither ordinary Heegaard stabilization nor basepoint-pair stabilization; their weighted target-neck operations are separate.

The handleslide maps are actual marked triangle counts. Their inverses and homotopies are finite polynomial matrices; no U-adic completion or inversion of a nonunit polynomial is used. An isotopy handles EVERY complementary generator pair created at a tangency, including possible positive-U reverse arrows.

Assume Countable Choice. Let complete balanced disk systems of rank $m=h+k-1$ on a genus-h surface belong to ONE specified handlebody, with one w and one z mark in every cut component, and with the same actual trivial arcs and marks. Realize a specified own-system handleslide and its sufficiently small auxiliary copies by the circular ribbon model of the named suppliers; take the other curve copies sufficiently small. A handleslide requires $m\ge2$. Small isotopy copies alone are allowed for $m\ge1$. The actual ribbon and its common exterior avoid all marks.

The full marked index-one differential of each required model pair kills its top generator. Both actual top-input, index-zero triangle products in the circular move construction equal the stated top output with coefficient one, with NO other output or positive marked term. These assertions hold over the polynomial ring with all individual w and z variables retained, and hence after setting every z variable equal to one. They hold for sufficiently small regular coherent protected perturbations of the model.

This applies to every actual balanced h,k, including dependent meridian lists and genus zero when the required number of curves exists. No inference is made about mixed-system triangles involving the opposite handlebody. The proof computes actual zero-Chern restrictions and same-corner index differences; it does not assume every formal degree-one periodic domain has a Whitney representative.

Assume Countable Choice. An ordinary Heegaard stabilization of an actual balanced multipointed knot diagram in S3, disjoint from the attaching curves, marks and actual knot arcs, gives a filtered chain homotopy equivalence of its full minus complexes over $R=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$. Take actual finite square-zero good endpoint counts: no nonconstant strip has index at most zero, and all index-one strips are regular. All positive z terms and individual marked variables are retained. Maps have relative Maslov degree zero, homotopies degree plus one, and are Alexander filtered after identifying the relative origins. This asserts no absolute centering or marked-pair stabilization.

For chosen data the nearest bijection $x\mapsto x\times c$ literally identifies the actual rigid counts, including their individual w and z vectors. The stabilized chosen path has no nonconstant nonpositive-index strip and has regular index-one strips. Independent good endpoint choices are compared by actual full-minus continuations. The proof solves the torus mean obstructions and exhausts changing-target limits; it does not assume a transverse split disk disjoint union of horizontal tori.

Assume Countable Choice. For an actual balanced multipointed S3 knot diagram with k ordered pairs, a marked-pair insertion in the elementary configuration of the pointed-data definition has the following full filtered minus chain type over $R'=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k,U_{k+1}]$:
$$\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(U_{k+1}+U_i:C[U_{k+1}]\longrightarrow C[U_{k+1}]\bigr).$$
Here C is the old actual full minus complex, i labels the old alpha cut component containing the removed connecting z-point, and the cone's source copy is shifted by $(-1,-1)$ in relative Maslov and Alexander degrees. All positive z terms are retained. For suitable good data this is the ACTUAL differential matrix, with diagonal d,d, indicated off-diagonal $U_{k+1}+U_i$ and zero reverse entry after setting every z variable to one. Independently chosen good complexes are related to it by actual finite filtered comparisons and inverse homotopies.

Restriction to any old chosen variable gives the old filtered chain type. Choosing the new variable gives the same type after its actual variable renaming; this uses polynomial divided differences and no completion. Ordinary simultaneous quotient identifies the cone with its zero-map specialization and contributes the two-dimensional factor of degrees $(0,0),(-1,-1)$. This statement concerns the actual insertion/removal along the represented knot, not adjoining a separated marked component.

The proof retains the extra closed horizontal surface in the old singly pointed case. Its count is not inferred from a zero unit-boundary count or erased by fixed-target sphere avoidance.

Let $R=\mathbb F_2[U,Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]$, and let $(C,d)$ be a graded, Alexander-filtered chain complex of free $R$-modules. Every variable has Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$, and $d$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not increase filtration. Extend scalars to $C[T]$, with $T$ having the same degrees. Put $f=T+U$ and form the cone $B=C[T]^{\mathrm{low}}\oplus C[T]$, with differential $D(a,b)=(da,db+fa)$; the first copy is shifted down by one in both Maslov degree and filtration. Regarded over $R$, this cone has an explicit filtered chain deformation retraction onto $C$. Its projection is evaluation of the second component at $T=U$, its inclusion is $c\mapsto(0,c)$, and its homotopy is polynomial divided difference in the second component, placed in the first component.

In contrast, the ordinary scalar quotient $T=U$ taken before homology gives the zero-map cone $C\oplus C^{\mathrm{low}}$, equivalently $C\otimes V$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Any further ordinary quotient of the old variables has the same direct-sum description with the corresponding quotient of $C$. Thus an equivalence of a basepoint insertion complex with this cone over the full polynomial ring implies invariance for the chosen single-variable action and an extra $V$ factor after simultaneous collapse. These are different operations.

More generally, let $E$ be free over $R[T]$ on a homogeneous filtered basis, and let its differential $d(T)$ have the same degree and filtration behavior, with polynomial matrix entries. Then $\operatorname{Cone}(T+U:E\to E)$ admits an explicit filtered deformation retraction over $R$ onto the ordinary quotient $(E/(T+U)E,d(U))$. If multiplication by $T+U$ on $E$ has a polynomial-linear homotopy $L$ with $dL+Ld=T+U$, Maslov degree $-1$, and filtration degree at most $-1$, this quotient is filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $R$ to $E\otimes V$. Iterating applies to independent marking variables and survives every earlier scalar quotient. Thus pairwise such homotopies imply that simultaneous collapse of $n$ variables to one has type $E\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ over the chosen variable action.

Assume countable choice. Let $f$ be an orientation-preserving isomorphism of two embedded multipointed diagrams in the sense of the admissible pointed-diagram definition, with $k$ ordered pairs and $m=h+k-1$. Transport the complex structure $j$, area form, protected neighborhoods and almost complex path $J_t$ by its surface restriction and the induced symmetric-product map $\Psi=\operatorname{Sym}^m(f|_\Sigma)$.

Then $\Psi$ bijects generators and Whitney classes, preserves every $w_i,z_i$ multiplicity and their region coefficients, and gives translation-equivariant bijections of the actual holomorphic-strip spaces. Their linearizations are conjugate by the transported bundle maps and connections, so Fredholmness, actual real index and surjectivity are equivalent. Finite quotient counts and the finiteness conditions in the Definition hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other. Whenever the count differential is defined, its operator is conjugated by the $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$-linear generator bijection
$$f_\#(\mathbf x)=\Psi(\mathbf x).$$
In particular if one side is a chain complex then so is the other and $f_\#$ is an actual chain isomorphism with inverse $(f^{-1})_\#$.

This isomorphism preserves the relative Maslov and Alexander formulas, and preserves the assigned gradings and filtration when the same normalization data are transported. It commutes with restriction to any single chosen variable action, every ordinary coefficient quotient and passage to the Alexander-associated-graded complexes. Transport of a chosen gradient vector field, its critical-ball modifications, plane-field extensions and Seifert surface preserves their first-Chern pairing normalization whenever those data are supplied. These assertions construct the isomorphism; they do not assert that an ambient isotopy induces the identity on generators or homology, or that two independently chosen almost complex paths have already been compared by continuation.

If instead the comparison changes only the connecting arcs and their simultaneous bridge witnesses by an allowed fixed-splitting arc normalization, keep the entire surface diagram and its analytic data identical. Then the generators, Whitney classes, actual operators, multiplicities and count sums are literally the same, and their identification is the identity whenever the sums are defined. The relative grading formulas and identical assigned normalization constants agree. This additional identity assertion does not construct vector-field or Seifert normalizations for arbitrary arc choices, or prove independence of such constructions.

Work in the smooth category inherited from the oriented-link convention. In particular, an embedded bridge witness disk means the image of a smooth rank-two embedding of a planar disk, with ordinary smooth boundary or smooth transverse corners at its two marked endpoints; smoothness at a boundary or corner means local smooth extension in its charts. Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $h$, let $k\ge1$, and put $m=h+k-1$. A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. A **$2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for $S^3$** consists of a splitting $S^3=U_{\alpha}\cup_{\Sigma}U_{\beta}$ into handlebodies, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves on $\Sigma$ that bound pairwise disjoint properly embedded disks in $U_{\alpha}$ and $U_{\beta}$, respectively, cutting each handlebody into exactly $k$ three-balls, and two ordered sets of distinct points $\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)$ and $\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ disjoint from the curves. Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. For a grid representing one knot, the basepoint pairs can be numbered cyclically in reverse order of travel along the oriented knot so that $w_i,z_i$ lie in the same component $A_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}$ lie in the same component $B_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$.

Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Comparisons also allow **arc normalizations in the fixed splitting**: a smooth isotopy of the represented oriented knot, supported near the ordered marks and fixing each mark, during which every open connecting arc stays in its original handlebody and the two simultaneous boundary-parallel witness systems are retained or replaced by embedded witnesses for those same arcs. The surface, attaching curves, marked points and compression disks stay fixed. Such a normalization may replace a tangential marked crossing by a transverse one; the original data are not required to have neat arcs. This is a change of knot representative relative to the fixed surface, not a diagram isomorphism carrying both objects. Analytic and assigned grading data depending on the fixed surface diagram can be kept identical; the corresponding generator and disk-count identification is then the identity. Existence of normalizations with the required witnesses is a separate geometric assertion, not part of this definition. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.

The $m$-fold symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)=\Sigma^m/S_m$ is the space of unordered $m$-tuples of points of $\Sigma$, where $S_m$ permutes coordinates. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ be the quotient map. The product tori are the images $\mathbb T_{\alpha}=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_m)$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_m)$. Their intersection points are the generators. A **Whitney disk class** $\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps from a disk to $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on $\mathbb T_{\alpha}$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}$ and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions with coefficients equal to local multiplicities. Write $n_{w_i}(\phi)$ and $n_{z_i}(\phi)$ for its local multiplicities at the marked points. An almost complex structure $J$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle with $J^2=-1$. Fix a complex structure $j$ and an area form on $\Sigma$. For $m>0$, choose a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ of nearly symmetric almost complex structures, constant near $t=0,1$: each $J_t$ agrees with the induced integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(j)$ on a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and of every divisor $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ for a chosen interior point $p$ of every complementary region, including every marked point, and tames the form descended from the product area form off that neighborhood. The path is a sufficiently small perturbation in this class. For $m=0$ the symmetric product is a point. Local multiplicities are intersection numbers with these divisors; positivity is a mathematical property to be proved, not an additional choice of disk counts. A $\mathbb J$-holomorphic strip representative is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_{\tau}u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(\tau,0)\in\mathbb T_{\alpha}$, $u(\tau,1)\in\mathbb T_{\beta}$, and limits $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$ as $\tau\to-\infty,+\infty$. Translation in $\tau$ defines an $\mathbb R$-action. The Maslov index $\mu(\phi)$ is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at a representative of $\phi$; the relative Maslov grading convention is $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y)=\mu(\phi)-2\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{w_i}(\phi)$, up to one overall additive constant.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain in the complementary regions whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves; its local multiplicity at a marked point is the coefficient of the containing region. The pointed diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain with $n_{w_i}=0$ for all $i$ has at least one positive and at least one negative region coefficient. A path $\mathbb J$ is **regular for a set of disk classes** when the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at every holomorphic-strip representative in those classes is surjective. For a path regular on the classes used, let $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)$ be the space of strip representatives. If, for each generator $\mathbf x$, only finitely many pairs $(\mathbf y,\phi)$ with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing$, $\mu(\phi)=1$, and $n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0$ for every $i$ occur, and each quotient is finite, the multipointed full filtered minus module is the free module over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$ generated by $\mathbb T_{\alpha}\cap\mathbb T_{\beta}$, with differential
$$\partial^-\mathbf x=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y),\;\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing\\\mu(\phi)=1,\; n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \forall i}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,U_1^{n_{w_1}(\phi)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(\phi)}\mathbf y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is the count modulo two of the zero-dimensional quotient when it is finite. Quotienting by all $U_i$ leaves the fully blocked multipointed chain complex (the hat chain complex when $k=1$), with terms only from classes satisfying $n_{w_i}=0$ for every $i$; its Alexander-filtered associated-graded complex further retains only classes with every $n_{z_i}=0$. The relative Alexander grading convention is $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)$, with an overall additive constant. Each $U_i$ lowers Maslov grading by two and Alexander filtration by one. In a grid diagram, $\Sigma=T^2$, $h=1$, $k=n$, and $m=n$; the horizontal circles are the $\alpha$-curves, the vertical circles are the $\beta$-curves, and the $w$-points and $z$-points are the $O$- and $X$-markings respectively.

Assume Countable Choice. Supply an embedded admissible DOUBLY pointed diagram for an oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, its compression disks and compatible Morse trajectory data, and a compact oriented Seifert surface $F$. Use the knot orientation from $w$ to $z$ in the alpha handlebody and from $z$ to $w$ in the beta handlebody. In positive genus let $x$ be a generator. In genus zero use the empty generator. There is an actual relative knot Spin-c lift $t_{w,z}(x)$ on the zero surgery $S^3_0(K)$, constructed with the following convention: on the knot exterior use the NEGATIVE of the compatible gradient after cancelling the index-one/index-two trajectories selected by $x$; across the zero-surgery solid torus use the zero-relative-Euler extension specified in the proof. Reversing this vector field convention would reverse its Alexander evaluation and is not silently permitted.

The integer
$$A_F(x)=\frac12\langle c_1(t_{w,z}(x)),[\widehat F]\rangle$$
is well defined, independent of the local extension and framing choices in that construction and of the choice of Seifert surface for the fixed oriented knot. For every actual Whitney class from $x$ to $y$,
$$A_F(x)-A_F(y)=n_z(\phi)-n_w(\phi).$$
The standard genus-zero unknot generator has value zero. The construction is carried by orientation-preserving isomorphisms of the supplied knot, surface and Morse data, and by a smooth mark-free attaching-curve isotopy with its followed generator. Swapping $w,z$ with the same underlying attaching systems gives $A_{z,w}(x)=-A_{w,z}(x)$; this is a statement about the actual Chern pairing, not a homological symmetry theorem. Its value can be computed as half the relative Euler number of the exterior perpendicular plane on $F\setminus N(K)$ with the explicit boundary frame in the proof; the solid-torus cap contributes zero.

Consequently this construction fixes the additive constant of the relative Alexander grading on every connected generator set. In an actual full filtered minus differential, including positive multiplicities at both basepoints, the term $U^{n_w(\phi)}y$ has Alexander level $A_F(x)-n_z(\phi)$. An exact finite matrix model of that diagram acquires its absolute grading by evaluating this Euler number at one generator and then using the relative differences. This last assertion does not claim that an uncalibrated numerical matrix or the relative grading alone already supplies that Euler evaluation. In particular, if an actual orientation-preserving diagram isomorphism exchanges the two marks, followed by a mark-free attaching-curve isotopy returning its generator to $y$ in the original diagram, then $A_F(x)=-A_F(y)$. If the relative calculation also gives $A_F(x)=A_F(y)$, both are zero. Arbitrary Heegaard-move comparison and a grid closed-form centering calculation are separate operations.

Let a finite DOUBLY pointed three-sphere knot diagram have its actual full filtered minus count complex, a consistent integer relative Maslov grading, and underlying one-pointed hat complex $C$ with $H(C;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$. Here the hat complex is obtained by setting $U=0$ and retaining ALL terms of zero $w$ multiplicity, including positive $z$ multiplicity; it is not the Alexander-associated-graded knot Floer complex. Under the ACω hypothesis of the closed-three-manifold invariance theorem, that theorem supplies the homology hypothesis whenever $C$ is one of its actual diagram count complexes. An exact finite computation of $C$ is an alternative way to supply it, without a choice assumption.

There is exactly one integer shift of the relative Maslov grading for which the nonzero hat homology class has degree zero. This is the normalized three-sphere Maslov grading. It gives the full minus differential degree $-1$ and $U$ degree $-2$, and the standard unknot generator has degree zero. Every homogeneous-relative-degree hat chain equivalence has degree zero after these normalizations. In particular an actual exact finite model of the disk differential has this grading once its total hat homology generator is identified; an arbitrary relative grading shift is not an absolute normalization.

This assertion neither constructs a diagram comparison nor proves an absolute rational grading or a four-dimensional cobordism degree formula for other three-manifolds. It fixes Maslov degree, not the independent additive Alexander constant.

Assume Countable Choice. Take two actual doubly pointed Heegaard diagrams of the same oriented knot in the oriented three-sphere, their compatible Morse and compression data, and good finite square-zero full minus count data as in the named move operations. Both diagrams have exactly ONE ordered pair w,z, possibly different genera. Use the actual negative-Morse exterior field with its zero-relative-Euler zero-surgery cap to define the integral Seifert-surface Alexander grading. Normalize the relative Maslov grading by placing the sole total zero-w hat homology generator in degree zero.

There are finite chain homotopy equivalences over F_2[U] between these full filtered minus complexes preserving these absolute conventions: the maps have Maslov degree zero, their inverse homotopies degree one, and every term U^a y of an actual count map from x satisfies A(y)-a=A(x)-n_z. In particular all positive z terms are retained. After U=0 the maps and both inverse homotopies are finite Alexander-filtered maps of the actual total hat complexes. They identify the first Alexander level detecting the total generator, and identify the associated-graded homology with its normalized Maslov parity.

This comparison is between doubly pointed analytic diagrams. It neither computes a finite diagram's Seifert Euler anchor nor supplies a grid-to-analytic comparison. No absolute multipointed cone-centering assertion is made.

Assume ACω. For every closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, the homology of the hat Heegaard Floer complex over $\mathbb F_2$ is independent, up to isomorphism, of the pointed admissible Heegaard diagram used to define it. The assertion is invariance of the group $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$; it does not assert a diagram-independent filtered chain homotopy type.

Let $U$ be the standard oriented unknot and take its genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram: $\Sigma=S^2$, each handlebody is a three-ball, there are no $\alpha$- or $\beta$-curves, and one $w$-point and one $z$-point are joined by trivial arcs in the two balls. The associated-graded hat chain complex has one generator, zero differential, and homology of rank one over $\mathbb F_2$. This is a computation for the stated diagram; it makes no invariance claim for other diagrams.

derivations.claim: Use [F1]'s actual finite word for the represented oriented knot. It includes precisely the move configurations and identifications in the Statement. Its witness preparation retains the broad smooth inputs; it does not assume initially neat crossings or bridge interiors missing the compression faces. Prove that the chosen variable does not matter on a FIXED diagram. For k>=2 retain [F2]'s finite polynomial matrix D(U,V). At V=1 put L_j=(partial D/partial V_j)|_(V=1). Differentiating the finite curvature identity gives dL_j+L_jd=U_j+U_(j-1), with indices cyclic. Each L_j has Maslov degree -1 and filtration degree at most -1: its terms have at least one z multiplicity and derivative removes one formal V factor, while their actual weighted outputs have filtration loss at least one. Sums of consecutive L_j therefore give the same homotopy for any U_i+U_l. These are actual finite count matrices; no multiplication action on homology is substituted for a chain homotopy. For k=1 no comparison is needed.

For an attaching isotopy or handleslide apply [F3], and for an ordinary genus change apply [F4] or its inverse. They are equivalences over the unchanged independent polynomial ring, before restriction or collapse. All positive z terms remain in their finite matrices. Choose the local count data supplied by each operation and use [F3]'s auxiliary comparisons at its two ends to connect to the vertex data chosen in step 1.1. At a marked-pair insertion use [F5]'s actual cone over R[U_new]. Its source copy has shift (-1,-1), and its matrix is the old d on each diagonal, U_new+U_i on the indicated off-diagonal and zero on the reverse diagonal after V=1. In particular the reverse full positive-z bigons cancel; they have not been omitted. Restrict to any old chosen variable. The monic-variable retraction evaluates U_new=U_i and gives the old complex, retaining its OTHER independent variables. If the selected variable is the new one, divide instead in the old U_i and apply the general polynomial-differential retraction; its quotient is the old complex with this action renamed. These retractions and their inverse homotopies are filtered, with finite divided differences. Their assertion is restriction of scalars, not the ordinary quotient before taking this cone. The inverse removal has the reverse equivalence.

Here is the actual chosen-action equivalence, including its infinite-rank restricted module. Introduce a polynomial variable T of degrees (-2,-1) and put E=C[T]. The two cones of T+U_i and T+U_l are filtered chain isomorphic by the triangular map (a,b) to (a,b+L a), where dL+Ld=U_i+U_l from step 1.2; its own inverse has the same formula. Choose an action along the finite word, using step 2.3 whenever the label must change. Steps 2.1–3.1 supply an equivalence at every operation over that single-variable ring. It proves no equality between that module and its ordinary collapsed quotient.

To compute the ordinary collapsed quotient, keep one selected U and impose the other relations U_j+U=0 successively. The filtered triangular cone isomorphism and general divided-difference retraction in [F5] therefore give C/(U_j+U) equivalent to C tensor V over the surviving ring at that stage. Fix the absolute doubly pointed origin by [F7]. It is the actual relative Spin-c field with the zero-framed Seifert cap stated here, and gives the displayed half-Chern evaluation and relative n_z-n_w law. For two doubly pointed diagrams use the k=1 word in [F1]; it needs no marked-pair equalization. [F7]'s finite exterior trajectory/meridian-cap calculation fixes zero affine shift for the actual attaching maps, while its cancelling-ball calculation fixes zero for ordinary stabilization at any allowed location. Thus this word's full filtered maps preserve A_F, not just an arbitrarily shifted relative grading. Every differential term has A(U^a y)=A(x)-n_z, including n_z>0. citations.quote: Let $G$ be a toroidal grid of grid number $n$ representing one oriented knot, and let $M_{\mathbb O}$, $M_{\mathbb X}$, and $A_G$ be the functions defined from its finite point sets and the pair-counting function $J$. Then $M_{\mathbb O}$ and $M_{\mathbb X}$ are integer-valued, and every rectangle $r$ from a grid state $\mathbf x$ to a grid state $\mathbf y$ satisfies $M_{\mathbb O}(\mathbf x)-M_{\mathbb O}(\mathbf y)=1-2n_{\mathbb O}(r)+2\#(\mathbf x\cap\operatorname{Int}r)$ and $M_{\mathbb X}(\mathbf x)-M_{\mathbb X}(\mathbf y)=1-2n_{\mathbb X}(r)+2\#(\mathbf x\cap\operatorname{Int}r)$. Consequently $A_G$ is integer-valued and $A_G(\mathbf x)-A_G(\mathbf y)=n_{\mathbb X}(r)-n_{\mathbb O}(r)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $G$ be an oriented knot grid of size $n\ge2$, with its actual flat torus and product generator end charts. Write $M_O,M_X$ and $A_G=(M_O-M_X)/2-(n-1)/2$ for the grid grading functions. For every actual continuous Whitney class $\phi:x\to y$ in $\operatorname{Sym}^n(T)$, define its domain and marked multiplicities by the relative point-divisor degrees of any smooth model. Its actual fixed-end Fredholm index $\mu(\phi)$, before source translation, satisfies
$$\mu(\phi)=M_O(x)-M_O(y)+2\sum_{i=1}^n n_{O_i}(\phi),$$
and
$$A_G(x)-A_G(y)=\sum_{i=1}^n n_{X_i}(\phi)-\sum_{i=1}^n n_{O_i}(\phi).$$
These identities hold for all realized classes, with positive, zero or negative marked multiplicities. In particular no condition $n_X=0$ is imposed. They remain valid for the actual linearized index of a smooth finite-energy holomorphic strip with generator ends and the protected product end data, under the auxiliary complex-structure homotopies in the suppliers.

Consequently, an actual index-one holomorphic strip counted with weight $\prod_i U_i^{n_{O_i}}$, if all its marked multiplicities are nonnegative, lowers $M_O$ by one and drops the $A_G$ filtration by exactly $\sum_i n_{X_i}$, when $U_i$ has bidegree $(-2,-1)$. This is the full filtered relative grading assertion, rather than only its zero-$X$ associated graded specialization. It does not assert existence or finiteness of counts, square-zero, move invariance, a grid-to-analytic equivalence, or identification of an absolute analytic grading normalization.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $G$ be a knot grid of size $n\ge2$ on its actual flat torus, with horizontal alpha and vertical beta circles and the product-integrable end data. Let $u:x\to y$ be any REALIZED continuous Whitney class, with integral domain $D$. At a grid vertex $v$ write $\nu_v(D)$ for one quarter of the sum of its four adjacent cell coefficients, and put $n_x(D)=\sum_{v\in x}\nu_v(D)$. Then its actual fixed-end real index before translation is
$$\mu(u)=n_x(D)+n_y(D).$$
This includes signed domains and positive marked degrees. If every cell coefficient is nonnegative and $\mu(u)=1$, then $x,y$ differ in exactly two points and $D$ is exactly one embedded torus rectangle from $x$ to $y$, of multiplicity one and with no state point in its interior. No exclusion of $O$ or $X$ marks is imposed. Its row and column intervals are both proper cyclic intervals, so it is an ordinary rectangle among the four choices for those changed corners.

This proves actual index and domain classification, not existence or uniqueness of holomorphic representatives, their count, equality of equal-domain homotopy classes, or a grid-to-analytic chain equivalence.

Assume Countable Choice. Take an actual knot grid of size $n\ge2$, its flat complex torus and the constant path $J_t=\operatorname{Sym}^n(j_{\mathrm{flat}})$. Use its actual row and column product tori, $w=O,z=X$, and their flat product generator charts. Every empty-state oriented rectangle $R:x\to y$, with arbitrary $O$ and $X$ markings in its interior, has exactly ONE orbit of actual finite-energy holomorphic strips of domain $R$ under longitudinal translation. That strip has actual fixed-end index one and its actual linearization is onto. Every actual index-one strip is one of these rectangle strips. Thus all actual index-one orbits, across all endpoints and classes, are finite and regular for this constant path.

Consequently the full filtered polynomial disk-count matrix for this chosen analytic datum is EXACTLY the full filtered grid differential, on the identical state basis over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each rectangle weighted by $\prod U_i^{O_i(R)}$ and filtration drop $n_X(R)$. It squares to zero by the finite rectangle-composition proof. Taking its zero-drop part gives the associated-graded minus matrix; then setting all variables to zero gives the tilde matrix. The identity preserves the relative Maslov and Alexander differences when assigned by the grid grading formulas.

This is a chosen-data analytic count and chain identification. It does not assert independence from auxiliary data, normalized absolute analytic gradings, a singly pointed reduction or its stable factors, move invariance, or identification with an independently constructed invariant. Equal-domain Whitney homotopy classes are not presumed equal: uniqueness is for actual strip orbits and therefore also accounts for every class represented by such a strip.

Let $G$ and $G'$ be one-component grid diagrams related by one of the following local moves. A cyclic permutation changes the planar cut of the toroidal grid by moving the first row or column to the last. A row commutation exchanges consecutive rows whose closed horizontal marking intervals are disjoint or strictly nested; a column commutation uses the same condition on vertical marking intervals. A stabilization replaces a marked cell by a two-by-two block with the original marking type in two opposite cells and the other type in a third cell, leaves the fourth cell empty, and inserts one row and one column, relocating the old companion markings so each new row and column has one mark of each type. Any of the four empty corners is allowed, and destabilization is the inverse move. Regard each full filtered minus complex returned by the grid-complex algorithm as a complex over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen marking variable $U_i$, retaining the other independent variables. The resulting complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, with equivalences preserving the Maslov grading and Alexander filtration. For each move, finite grid-domain counts give filtered chain maps in both directions and filtered chain homotopies from both composites to the identity. For a stabilization, its multivariable target is first compared with the cone of $U_{n+1}+U_i$ on the polynomial extension of the original complex. After instead taking the simultaneous ordinary quotient $U_1=\cdots=U_n=U$, a stabilization contributes a zero-map cone, equivalently an extra zero-differential factor $V$; those fully collapsed complexes are compared with this factor retained. Under commutation the tilde homologies are isomorphic; under a stabilization from grid number $n$ to $n+1$, the tilde homology changes by tensoring with the two-dimensional bigraded vector space $V$ with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $G_0,G_1$ be finite planar grid diagrams, with vertical segments over horizontal segments and orientation from $O$ to $X$ in rows and $X$ to $O$ in columns, representing the same oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. A cyclic permutation moves the first row or column to the last position. A row commutation exchanges adjacent rows when the closed intervals between their respective $O$- and $X$-mark abscissae are disjoint or one lies in the interior of the other; a column commutation is defined by the same condition on the intervals between marking heights. A stabilization chooses a marked cell and temporarily removes its marking together with the other markings in its row and column. It splits that row and column into two, places the three removed markings, and adds one new $O$-mark and one new $X$-mark so that every row and column again has one of each. In the four-cell subdivision of the chosen cell, exactly three cells are marked: the chosen marking type appears twice, the other type once, and any one corner may be the empty cell; the two other markings removed from the original row and column are placed outside this block in the new row and column. A destabilization is the inverse operation. Then a finite sequence of cyclic permutations, commutations, stabilizations, and destabilizations carries $G_0$ to $G_1$.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix one actual balanced multipointed diagram of an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $k\ge1$, $m=h+k-1$ and its ordered marks. Take two actual finite square-zero full minus count complexes over $R=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$, with all positive z degrees retained. Suppose their chosen end paths have no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and every index-one strip is regular, as in the full-marked chosen-count construction. Background surface complex structures, positive area forms, full torus tensors and optional generator charts may have been chosen independently.

There are finite actual anchored continuation matrices over R and inverse chain homotopies. They are filtered for the relative Alexander filtration and homogeneous for the relative Maslov degree, after identifying the origins on the SAME geometric generator set. Every $U_i$ has degrees $(-2,-1)$. Positive z terms are included and lower filtration by their total z degree; no associated-graded substitution is made. Scalar restriction to any chosen variable, or identification or localization of variables, preserves these actual finite identities.

The proof supplies compact low-dimensional continuation spaces and their exhaustive collars by an actual full-marked index budget. No zero-basepoint bubble exclusion is substituted for that budget. No comparison of different attaching systems, genus changes, basepoint-pair cones or absolute normalization is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, let $F$ be a compact connected oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible multipointed Heegaard diagrams for $K$. For $i=0,1$, the diagram $\mathcal H_i$ has a closed genus-$h_i$ Heegaard surface and $m_i=h_i+k_i-1$ curves in each attaching system, with $k_i$ ordered $w$-points and $k_i$ ordered $z$-points; each component of either attaching-system complement contains one point of each type, and the connecting arcs represent $K$. A curve isotopy is an isotopy of one attaching curve through embedded curves in its attaching system, disjoint from the other attaching curves and all marked points. A handleslide replaces one attaching curve by its band sum with another curve in the same attaching system, along an embedded arc disjoint from the other attaching curves and the marked points. A Heegaard stabilization forms connected sum with the genus-one splitting of $S^3$ in a disk disjoint from all curves, marked points, and knot arcs; it raises the genus by one and leaves $k$ fixed. A basepoint-pair (index-zero/three) stabilization keeps the genus fixed and adds one curve to each system and one $w,z$ pair along the represented knot. Its inverse removes the following elementary configuration, after relabeling the cyclic pairs: curves $\alpha_0,\beta_0$ bound disks $A_0,B_0$ on the surface, are disjoint from every opposite-system curve except each other, and intersect transversely in two points; $A_0\cap B_0$ is a bigon containing just $w_0$, while $A_0\setminus B_0$ contains just $z_0$ and $B_0\setminus A_0$ contains the next $z$-point along the cyclic pairing. Remove $\alpha_0,\beta_0,w_0,z_0$ and concatenate the adjacent trivial knot arcs. The surviving marked points stay fixed. Thus the move inserts a pair along an existing knot arc rather than adjoining an isolated marked component in an empty disk. Both descriptions include the simultaneous boundary-parallel arc systems and require the stated one-$w$, one-$z$ condition in each attaching complement. Destabilizations are the respective inverse moves. Comparisons may apply the orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms of the pointed-data definition, carrying the ordered marked points, attaching systems and simultaneous boundary-parallel arcs, before or after the listed geometric moves. Their complex identifications are induced by pushforward of generators, disk classes and almost complex data, rather than by assuming an isotopy acts as the identity. Comparisons also allow the fixed-splitting arc normalizations in that definition before or after the listed moves, retaining the simultaneous bridge witnesses and all ordered marks. They leave the surface attaching and analytic data fixed, so their identification of the actual count operators is the identity; they do not assert a diffeomorphism of a tangential and transverse surface-knot pair. With these identifications, any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of the listed moves through admissible multipointed diagrams, preserving the represented oriented knot.

For a diagram with $j$ basepoint pairs, regard its full filtered minus complex as a complex over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by restriction of scalars along $U\mapsto U_i$ for any one chosen basepoint variable. The resulting complexes of $\mathcal H_0$ and $\mathcal H_1$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, preserving relative Maslov grading and Alexander filtration, even when the diagrams have different numbers of basepoint pairs. The choice of the single variable action does not affect this type. Restriction retains the independent variables in the chain module; it is different from quotienting by $U_1=\cdots=U_j$. The latter ordinary quotient is the fully collapsed complex and has filtered chain homotopy type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Equivalently, a basepoint stabilization before quotienting is modeled by the cone of $U_{j+1}+U_i$ on the polynomial extension of the old complex; after the simultaneous quotient this is a zero-map cone and contributes the displayed extra factor.

For an admissible doubly-pointed diagram $\mathcal H_1$ for $(K,F)$, define $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ to be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from its full filtered minus complex by quotienting by its sole variable $U$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ use the Alexander grading
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned by the pointed Heegaard construction from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, and $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood of $K$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached so that this longitude bounds it (zero-framed surgery). The vector-field representative is extended across small balls around the critical points, and its first Chern class is the Chern class of the orthogonal oriented plane field. Use the absolute Maslov normalization in which the unique generator of $\widehat{HF}(S^3)$ has degree zero.

For a diagram $\mathcal H$ with $j$ basepoint pairs, let $\widetilde C(\mathcal H)$ be the Alexander-associated-graded complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from its full filtered minus complex by setting every $U_i=0$; its differential therefore counts only classes with all $n_{w_i}=n_{z_i}=0$. Its homology is $\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V=\mathbb F_2\langle v_0,v_1\rangle$ has bidegrees $(M,A)(v_0)=(0,0)$ and $(M,A)(v_1)=(-1,-1)$.

Let $R=\mathbb F_2[U,Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]$, and let $(C,d)$ be a graded, Alexander-filtered chain complex of free $R$-modules. Every variable has Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$, and $d$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not increase filtration. Extend scalars to $C[T]$, with $T$ having the same degrees. Put $f=T+U$ and form the cone $B=C[T]^{\mathrm{low}}\oplus C[T]$, with differential $D(a,b)=(da,db+fa)$; the first copy is shifted down by one in both Maslov degree and filtration. Regarded over $R$, this cone has an explicit filtered chain deformation retraction onto $C$. Its projection is evaluation of the second component at $T=U$, its inclusion is $c\mapsto(0,c)$, and its homotopy is polynomial divided difference in the second component, placed in the first component.

In contrast, the ordinary scalar quotient $T=U$ taken before homology gives the zero-map cone $C\oplus C^{\mathrm{low}}$, equivalently $C\otimes V$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Any further ordinary quotient of the old variables has the same direct-sum description with the corresponding quotient of $C$. Thus an equivalence of a basepoint insertion complex with this cone over the full polynomial ring implies invariance for the chosen single-variable action and an extra $V$ factor after simultaneous collapse. These are different operations.

More generally, let $E$ be free over $R[T]$ on a homogeneous filtered basis, and let its differential $d(T)$ have the same degree and filtration behavior, with polynomial matrix entries. Then $\operatorname{Cone}(T+U:E\to E)$ admits an explicit filtered deformation retraction over $R$ onto the ordinary quotient $(E/(T+U)E,d(U))$. If multiplication by $T+U$ on $E$ has a polynomial-linear homotopy $L$ with $dL+Ld=T+U$, Maslov degree $-1$, and filtration degree at most $-1$, this quotient is filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $R$ to $E\otimes V$. Iterating applies to independent marking variables and survives every earlier scalar quotient. Thus pairwise such homotopies imply that simultaneous collapse of $n$ variables to one has type $E\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ over the chosen variable action.

Let a finite DOUBLY pointed three-sphere knot diagram have its actual full filtered minus count complex, a consistent integer relative Maslov grading, and underlying one-pointed hat complex $C$ with $H(C;\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$. Here the hat complex is obtained by setting $U=0$ and retaining ALL terms of zero $w$ multiplicity, including positive $z$ multiplicity; it is not the Alexander-associated-graded knot Floer complex. Under the ACω hypothesis of the closed-three-manifold invariance theorem, that theorem supplies the homology hypothesis whenever $C$ is one of its actual diagram count complexes. An exact finite computation of $C$ is an alternative way to supply it, without a choice assumption.

There is exactly one integer shift of the relative Maslov grading for which the nonzero hat homology class has degree zero. This is the normalized three-sphere Maslov grading. It gives the full minus differential degree $-1$ and $U$ degree $-2$, and the standard unknot generator has degree zero. Every homogeneous-relative-degree hat chain equivalence has degree zero after these normalizations. In particular an actual exact finite model of the disk differential has this grading once its total hat homology generator is identified; an arbitrary relative grading shift is not an absolute normalization.

This assertion neither constructs a diagram comparison nor proves an absolute rational grading or a four-dimensional cobordism degree formula for other three-manifolds. It fixes Maslov degree, not the independent additive Alexander constant.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Assume Countable Choice. Supply an embedded admissible DOUBLY pointed diagram for an oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, its compression disks and compatible Morse trajectory data, and a compact oriented Seifert surface $F$. Use the knot orientation from $w$ to $z$ in the alpha handlebody and from $z$ to $w$ in the beta handlebody. In positive genus let $x$ be a generator. In genus zero use the empty generator. There is an actual relative knot Spin-c lift $t_{w,z}(x)$ on the zero surgery $S^3_0(K)$, constructed with the following convention: on the knot exterior use the NEGATIVE of the compatible gradient after cancelling the index-one/index-two trajectories selected by $x$; across the zero-surgery solid torus use the zero-relative-Euler extension specified in the proof. Reversing this vector field convention would reverse its Alexander evaluation and is not silently permitted.

The integer
$$A_F(x)=\frac12\langle c_1(t_{w,z}(x)),[\widehat F]\rangle$$
is well defined, independent of the local extension and framing choices in that construction and of the choice of Seifert surface for the fixed oriented knot. For every actual Whitney class from $x$ to $y$,
$$A_F(x)-A_F(y)=n_z(\phi)-n_w(\phi).$$
The standard genus-zero unknot generator has value zero. The construction is carried by orientation-preserving isomorphisms of the supplied knot, surface and Morse data, and by a smooth mark-free attaching-curve isotopy with its followed generator. Swapping $w,z$ with the same underlying attaching systems gives $A_{z,w}(x)=-A_{w,z}(x)$; this is a statement about the actual Chern pairing, not a homological symmetry theorem. Its value can be computed as half the relative Euler number of the exterior perpendicular plane on $F\setminus N(K)$ with the explicit boundary frame in the proof; the solid-torus cap contributes zero.

Consequently this construction fixes the additive constant of the relative Alexander grading on every connected generator set. In an actual full filtered minus differential, including positive multiplicities at both basepoints, the term $U^{n_w(\phi)}y$ has Alexander level $A_F(x)-n_z(\phi)$. An exact finite matrix model of that diagram acquires its absolute grading by evaluating this Euler number at one generator and then using the relative differences. This last assertion does not claim that an uncalibrated numerical matrix or the relative grading alone already supplies that Euler evaluation. In particular, if an actual orientation-preserving diagram isomorphism exchanges the two marks, followed by a mark-free attaching-curve isotopy returning its generator to $y$ in the original diagram, then $A_F(x)=-A_F(y)$. If the relative calculation also gives $A_F(x)=A_F(y)$, both are zero. Arbitrary Heegaard-move comparison and a grid closed-form centering calculation are separate operations.

Every toroidal grid diagram representing a knot is an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram in the stated knot Floer convention: each nonzero periodic domain with zero local multiplicity at every $O$-marking has both positive and negative region coefficients.

For every one-component toroidal grid and each of the tilde, associated-graded minus, and full filtered minus modes, the differential defined by the grid-complex algorithm satisfies $\partial^2=0$ over its stated coefficient ring.

The **grid-complex algorithm** takes a finite encoded grid and a mode from $\{\mathrm{tilde},\mathrm{minus\text{-}associated\text{-}graded},\mathrm{minus\text{-}filtered}\}$. It requires an integer grid number $n\ge2$, disjoint $O$- and $X$-markings with exactly one of each in every row and column, and an induced component permutation that is one $n$-cycle. If $n<2$ or the marking conditions fail, return `invalid-grid`; if the component permutation has more than one cycle, return `link-input-not-supported`. No chain complex is returned on either branch.

For a valid knot grid, number the horizontal and vertical circles $1,\ldots,n$ and enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ in lexicographic order. The state for a permutation $\sigma$ consists of the $n$ intersections $(i,\sigma(i))$. For each ordered pair of states $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$, if they agree in other than exactly $n-2$ points, add no rectangle terms. Otherwise enumerate the at most two torus rectangles with the four nonshared state points as corners, retain those whose interiors contain no point of $\mathbf x$, and apply the selected mode. In the full filtered mode, each term drops filtration by $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$; the associated-graded mode retains precisely the terms with zero drop, which are the rectangles with no $X$-marking:

1. **Tilde mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2$. Count a retained rectangle with coefficient $1$ exactly when its interior contains no $O$- or $X$-marking.
2. **Associated-graded minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count a retained rectangle exactly when its interior contains no $X$-marking, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$.
3. **Full filtered minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count every retained rectangle, regardless of its $X$-markings, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$. Use the grid Alexander value for each state and assign filtration drop $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$ to this term.

Return the ordered state list, the mode and coefficient ring, the exact differential matrix obtained by summing coefficients modulo two, the state Maslov and Alexander values, and the filtration data for the full filtered mode. The algorithm returns this finite presentation only; its identification with knot Floer homology and its independence of the chosen grid are separate theorems. The factor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ is not multiplied into the output.

derivations.claim: Use the standard genus-one splitting of the oriented three-sphere: the horizontal circles bound parallel meridian disks in one solid torus, and the vertical circles bound parallel meridian disks in the other; their primitive meridians meet once. Taking all n parallel disks cuts each side into n balls. The row and column marking condition puts one O and one X in every corresponding cut ball. Push the horizontal O-to-X segments into the lower side and the vertical X-to-O segments into the upper side, using their evident rectangular bridge disks. These simultaneous arcs give exactly the oriented knot of the grid, since every vertical segment passes over every horizontal segment. Thus this is an actual balanced 2n-pointed diagram of K, not only an abstract torus count. Its analytic symmetric rank is $1+n-1=n$, and w=O,z=X. Give it the actual flat integrable data of [F1]. The identity on states identifies its full polynomial count matrix with the algorithmic one.

Check the remaining good-endpoint condition before applying [F3]. Positivity gives a nonnegative domain D for every actual integrable strip. Its index $n_x(D)+n_y(D)$ is nonnegative. If it is zero, every cell touching either state has coefficient zero. The local equation $\Delta D=1_x-1_y$ then forces x=y, since at any changed vertex the four coefficients would have nonzero alternating sum. Consequently $\Delta D=0$, and telescoping its row and column differences gives $D_{ij}=a_i+b_j$. Because x is one point in every row and column, the n cells immediately northeast of its state points have total coefficient $\sum_i a_i+\sum_j b_j=0$. The sum of ALL cell coefficients is n times that sum, hence zero. Nonnegativity gives D=0. The actual ordered-root energy bound is then zero, so the strip is constant. Therefore no nonconstant index-at-most-zero strip exists. Finiteness, index-one regularity and square zero were already supplied by [F1,F5]; no index-two regularity of this special integrable path is assumed. The precise endpoint hypotheses of [F3] hold.

Apply the actual full-minus auxiliary and diagram equivalences of [F3] to this endpoint. They identify its chosen-action restriction with a doubly pointed full complex, and identify its ordinary collapse with that complex tensor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$. They also give the quotient-by-all-variables and associated-graded identities by specializing the actual finite maps and homotopies. At this stage use ONLY the relative formulas of [F1]: on the connected state set, its numerical J-gradings differ from the transported normalized analytic origins by one integer Maslov constant b and one integer Alexander constant c. In particular, if H denotes normalized doubly pointed associated-graded zero-U homology, the grid tilde homology has the relative identification $H\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ with common shifts (b,c). This constructs the comparison before determining either shift; no assertion of the theorem under proof is a premise.

Fix b without using Alexander centering. List the O markings in order of increasing row, with distinct column indices $o_0,\ldots,o_{n-1}$. Replace X by $X^*$ having in row i the column $o_{i+1}$, with cyclic indices. This is disjoint from O and is a one-component grid: its marking permutation sends row i to row i+1. Its vertical segments join successive row heights, except for the one segment from the last row to the first. The short vertical segments meet no other horizontal height, so every crossing lies on that sole long vertical segment, which passes OVER the complementary embedded planar arc. This is an unknot: raise the long segment into an upper ball and lower the complementary planar arc into a lower ball; both are boundary-parallel arcs, with the rectangular upper bridge disk and the planar lower bridge disk. Match their boundary chords on the separating plane and join the two disks along that chord to obtain an embedded spanning disk, rounding its finite corners. The FULL unfiltered rectangle matrix and M_O do not depend on X, so replacing X by $X^*$ changes neither this matrix nor its Maslov grading. By the purely combinatorial graded chosen-action equivalences and move generation in [F2], this same unfiltered complex is graded equivalent to a size-two unknot grid. In that grid the two states have M_O=0,-1; direct rectangle enumeration gives the cone $\mathbb F_2[U_1,U_2]\xrightarrow{U_1+U_2}\mathbb F_2[U_1,U_2]$ with source degree -1 and target degree zero. The monic polynomial retraction in [F3] evaluates the other variable at the chosen one, so after quotienting that chosen U its total homology is one-dimensional in M_O degree zero. The combinatorial inverse homotopies specialize too, so this is true for the original grid's chosen-action total zero-U complex. Step 3.1 compares it to the analytic total hat homology, whose normalized degree is zero by [F4]. Its common Maslov shift is therefore b=0. This also proves nontriviality without treating the Alexander-associated-graded complex as total hat homology.

Fix c by a finite reciprocal symmetry. Define the finite Laurent polynomial $P_G(t)=\sum_x(-1)^{M_O(x)}t^{A_G(x)}$ and put $D_n(t)=(1-t^{-1})^{n-1}$. The Euler characteristic of a finite bigraded complex equals that of its homology degree by degree: split each finite degree into boundaries, a homology complement and a complement mapped isomorphically to boundaries; the latter pairs cancel with opposite Maslov signs. Thus [F2] implies that $Q_G=P_G/D_n$ is unchanged by every grid move, as a rational function: commutation preserves P and stabilization multiplies P by $1-t^{-1}$, precisely the Euler polynomial of V. Construct $G^T$ by transposing the square and INTERCHANGING O and X. The ambient rotation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(y,x,-z)$ has determinant plus one and changes old vertical overpasses to new horizontal underpasses. An old horizontal O-to-X arc becomes a new vertical X-to-O arc; an old vertical X-to-O arc becomes a new horizontal O-to-X arc. Hence it carries the SAME oriented knot to $G^T$, rather than a mirror or assumed orientation reversal. Both grids have size n, so [F2] gives $P_{G^T}=P_G$. Transposition preserves the strict pair relation defining J, while mark exchange swaps M_O and M_X. The literal formulas are therefore $A_{G^T}(x^T)=-A_G(x)-(n-1)$ and $M_{O^T}(x^T)=M_O(x)-2A_G(x)-(n-1)$. Since A_G is integral, their signs give $P_G(t)=(-1)^{n-1}t^{-(n-1)}P_G(t^{-1})$. Using $D_n(t^{-1})=(-1)^{n-1}t^{n-1}D_n(t)$ yields $Q_G(t)=Q_G(t^{-1})$. This derives reciprocity from actual J formulas and purely combinatorial moves; no analytic grading identification or unproved Alexander determinant formula has been used.

Write $Q_H(t)=\sum_{m,a}(-1)^m\dim H_{m,a}\,t^a$. This is a finite Laurent polynomial. By [F4]'s ACTUAL conjugation, $H_{m,a}$ is isomorphic to $H_{m-2a,-a}$. The degree difference is even, hence $Q_H(t)=Q_H(t^{-1})$. For clarity, this symmetry is supplied by the normalized analytic coordinate-swap map: on the vertical corner $(i,j)=(0,a)$ it lands on the horizontal corner $(a,0)$, and multiplying by $U^a$ identifies that corner with $(0,-a)$ and lowers Maslov degree by 2a. It is a map of the corner subquotients, not a declaration that the full positive-z hat differential preserves A. Moreover $Q_H(1)=1$. Indeed the associated graded and total zero-U doubly pointed complexes have the same finite chain groups with their Maslov degrees, so their ordinary Euler characteristics coincide; the latter has exactly one homology class of normalized degree zero. Therefore Q_H is NONZERO. The relative comparison in step 3.1 and b=0 now give $P_G=t^c D_n Q_H$, or $Q_G=t^c Q_H$. Substituting the two reciprocal identities yields $(t^c-t^{-c})Q_H=0$ in the Laurent polynomial domain $\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$. Since Q_H is nonzero, c=0. This is precisely the missing absolute combinatorial Alexander anchor, with no appeal to grid equality to establish its own shift.

The identity in step 1.1 and the actual analytic equivalences in step 3.1 consequently preserve both normalized origins, by steps 4.1 and 5.1. Compose with [F3]'s normalized comparison to the diagram H in the Statement; its inverse and inverse homotopies remain finite and filtered. Taking the Alexander associated graded of these identities gives the claimed associated-graded minus equivalences. Each term retains every individual O weight until the explicitly stated restriction or quotient. The ordinary collapse and all-variable-zero associated-graded specialization are exactly the two actual constructions of [F3], yielding respectively $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ and $\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$, with the displayed bidegrees now absolutely centered. The chosen-action restriction yields $CFK^-(K)$ instead. Composing the comparisons for two grids gives their normalized filtered equivalence and inverse homotopies. Finally [F4] identifies the preserved Alexander origin with the zero-framed capped-Seifert half-Chern expression of the Statement. Its cap and negative-Morse convention are inherited from that supplier, not replaced by a winding-number convention. Every original conclusion follows with all positive z terms and all stated scalar distinctions retained.

citations.quote:
Work in the smooth category inherited from the oriented-link convention. In particular, an embedded bridge witness disk means the image of a smooth rank-two embedding of a planar disk, with ordinary smooth boundary or smooth transverse corners at its two marked endpoints; smoothness at a boundary or corner means local smooth extension in its charts. Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $h$, let $k\ge1$, and put $m=h+k-1$. A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. A **$2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for $S^3$** consists of a splitting $S^3=U_{\alpha}\cup_{\Sigma}U_{\beta}$ into handlebodies, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves on $\Sigma$ that bound pairwise disjoint properly embedded disks in $U_{\alpha}$ and $U_{\beta}$, respectively, cutting each handlebody into exactly $k$ three-balls, and two ordered sets of distinct points $\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)$ and $\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ disjoint from the curves. Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. For a grid representing one knot, the basepoint pairs can be numbered cyclically in reverse order of travel along the oriented knot so that $w_i,z_i$ lie in the same component $A_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}$ lie in the same component $B_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$.

Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification.
